cases.situation: I've been fighting a flaky Cypress test for two hours and Jonas wrote most of that test suite. We're peers, he's busy with the release too. How do I ask him without sounding helpless?
cases.reply: Hey Jonas, the checkout Cypress test is failing about one run in three and I've spent two hours on it. I've ruled out the test data and the retry config, and it only fails in CI, not locally. Could you pair with me for 15 minutes this afternoon? If you're buried in the release, tomorrow morning works too.
cases.note: Showing the two things already ruled out turns 'help me' into 'help me finish', and 15 minutes is easy to say yes to.

cases.situation: 我是组长，想把下个月客户年会的物料统筹交给新来的同事小周，她之前在上一家公司做过活动。怎么说才不像甩锅？
cases.reply: 小周，想请你来负责11月18号客户年会的全部物料统筹。你之前做过好几场活动，这块你比组里其他人都熟。完成的标准是：11月8号前把展架、手册和伴手礼都定稿下单，预算控制在3万以内。初稿出来我随时帮你过一遍，我也会跟王经理说好，这件事正式算在你的工作量里。你看现在手上的事情，接得下来吗？
cases.note: 说清结果、为什么是她、完成标准和截止日，最后真心问一句她接不接得住，而不是直接派活。

cases.situation: In a meeting with the VP today she asked me what our churn rate was for enterprise accounts last quarter and I blanked. I want to send a follow-up on Slack.
cases.reply: Hi Carla, on your question about enterprise churn in Q2: I didn't have the number in my head and didn't want to guess. I'm pulling it from the billing data with Ahmed now and will send you the exact figure, with the three biggest accounts we lost, by 4pm today. Is this for the board deck, or something else I should shape it for?
cases.note: The 'I don't know' formula: say it cleanly, name the next step and a time, and ask what the answer feeds into.
